beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Let's add these two numbers, starting at the ones.

do.text: Ten here becomes one next door

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each counter is worth the number above its column: a thousand, a hundred, ten, or one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Put both numbers together, matching their places. Start at the ones; each trade can change the column to its left.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Eight plus three is eleven ones. Trade ten ones for one ten. One one stays.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Seven tens, plus two tens, plus our carried ten: ten tens. Trade them for one hundred. Zero tens stay.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Seven hundreds, plus six, plus the carried one: fourteen hundreds. Trade ten for one thousand. Four hundreds stay.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Five thousands, plus one, plus the carried one: seven thousands.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Seven thousand, four hundred one. The same trade happened three times!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: We call that regrouping: changing the groups without changing the amount.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Let's subtract. This time, we trade in the other direction.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Three ones. Can I take seven minus three instead?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Keep the order. Trade for more ones.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The tens and hundreds are empty. Go left to a place that has something to trade.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Open one thousand into ten hundreds. Four thousands stay.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Keep nine hundreds. Open the tenth hundred into ten tens.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Keep nine tens. Open the tenth ten into ten ones. Together with our three, that makes thirteen ones.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Each middle column received ten, then gave one onward. That is why nine stayed!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Count the value: four thousand, nine hundred, ninety, and thirteen. Still five thousand three.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Only the groups changed. Now take away seven ones from thirteen. Six remain.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Nine tens minus four tens leaves five tens.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Nine hundreds minus three hundreds leaves six hundreds.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four thousands minus one thousand leaves three thousands.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Three thousand, six hundred fifty-six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Add back what we took away to check our subtraction.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Six plus seven is thirteen. Write three; carry one ten.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Five plus four plus one is ten. Zero tens; carry one hundred.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Six plus three plus one is ten. Zero hundreds; carry one thousand.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three plus one plus one is five. Five thousand three, exactly where we started.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Six places. Watch the same trades ripple through a larger addition.

do.text: The same step in six places

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ones: six plus nine is fifteen. Write five, carry one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Tens: one plus two plus one is four.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Hundreds: five plus nine is fourteen. Write four, carry one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Thousands: eight plus three plus one is twelve. Write two, carry one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten thousands: four plus seven plus one is twelve. Write two, carry one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Hundred thousands: two plus one plus one is four.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four hundred twenty-two thousand, four hundred forty-five.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A carry beyond the left edge starts a new place.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Add a shorter number: eight hundred sixty-two.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: If I line up the left edges, my eight lands under ten thousands. But it means eight hundreds!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Slide the whole number right. Two ones under five ones; six tens under one ten; eight hundreds under four hundreds.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Now add. Five plus two is seven.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One plus six is seven.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four plus eight is twelve hundreds. Write two and carry one thousand.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Zero plus the carried one is one thousand.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three ten thousands stay.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Thirty-one thousand, two hundred seventy-seven. Match the places, whatever the lengths.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Your turn. Where should the trades stop in this subtraction?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: The ones are ready: four minus three is one.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: The tens need help. I go past the empty hundreds to the thousands.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: One thousand opens into ten hundreds. Five thousands stay.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: One hundred opens into ten tens. Nine hundreds stay.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Stop at the tens. They keep all ten because the ones did not need a trade.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Ten tens minus three tens is seven tens.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Nine hundreds minus four hundreds is five hundreds.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Five thousands minus three thousands is two thousands. My answer is two thousand, five hundred seventy-one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One thousand can open into ten hundreds.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One of those hundreds can open into ten tens.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One of those tens can open into ten ones.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten here is one there, in every column.
